title: Langmuir waves
what: An eerie, wavering tone: electrons in the solar wind oscillating at the plasma frequency, picked up by the FIELDS electric antennas and shifted into hearing range.
credit: NASA/Johns Hopkins APL; Parker Solar Probe FIELDS

title: Whistler-mode waves
what: Sci-fi swoops and whirs: energetic electrons spiralling out of the corona along magnetic field lines amplify a plasma wave that matches their spin, recorded by FIELDS.
credit: NASA/Johns Hopkins APL; Parker Solar Probe FIELDS

title: Dispersive chirping waves
what: Rushing, wind-on-a-microphone chirps: plasma waves that slide quickly from one frequency to another, rare near Earth but everywhere close to the Sun, recorded by FIELDS.
credit: NASA/Johns Hopkins APL; Parker Solar Probe FIELDS

title: Ion-cyclotron waves (raw audification)
what: A buzzing, warbling band over a hiss: the magnetic field wobbling as solar-wind ions gyrate (ion-scale cyclotron waves), heard by playing FIELDS magnetometer samples straight through as audio, about 75 minutes of data per 30 seconds.
credit: NASA SPDF/CDAWeb; Parker Solar Probe FIELDS (PSP_FLD_L2_MAG_RTN, tangential component)

title: Venus’ ionosphere hum
what: A low rumble that rises to a high whir and falls back: a natural low-frequency radio emission FIELDS caught while Parker skimmed through Venus’ upper atmosphere during its third flyby, 833 km above the surface.
credit: NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center/Mark SubbaRao; data: Parker Solar Probe FIELDS, Glyn Collinson (CUA)
